title: Minimum Cost to Make All Characters Equal
summary: Given a 0-indexed binary string s of length n , you can perform the following operations: - Choose an index i and invert all characters from index 0 to index i (inclusive), with a cost of i + 1 .
statement: Given a 0-indexed binary string s of length n , you can perform the following operations: - Choose an index i and invert all characters from index 0 to index i (inclusive), with a cost of i + 1 . - Choose an index i and invert all characters from index i to index n - 1 (inclusive), with a cost of n - i . Determine the minimum cost required to make all characters in the string identical.
constraints: In one operation, choose a prefix or suffix, flip every bit in it, and pay its length.
Make every character equal, choosing either all zeroes or all ones.
Return the minimum total operation cost.
hints: Only boundaries where adjacent bits differ need to be eliminated.
For a boundary at index i, flip either its i-character prefix or its n-i-character suffix.
Add min(i,n-i) independently for every adjacent transition.
Each flip toggles whether exactly one selected boundary crosses its endpoint; paying the nearer endpoint realizes every required boundary at minimum cost.
